the Ca(2+)(i) transients induced by photolytic release of InsP3 are composed of distinct phases, that these phases reflect mainly intracelluar redistribution of the ion and that the initial rate of Ca(2+)((i) rise and the delay of Ca(2+)((i) upstroke is correlated with the amount liberated InsP3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intracellular Ca2+ in the process of oocyte maturation.
the role of Ca(2+), InsP(3) and InsP(4) in mouse oocytes.
the role of intracellular calcium in oocyte maturation, fertilization and embryogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
InsP3-induced [Ca2+]i transients in mouse oocytes are complex and are the result of a series of Ca(2+ )reactions involving both intracellular and extracellular Ca2+ pools.
InsP3 induces a transient release of Ca2+ from the InsP3 sensitive stores which is sufficient to trigger a Ca2+-induced Ca2+-release process from the InsP1-sensitive stores.
the Ca2+ signal transduction in mouse oocytes involves both InsP3-sensitive Ca2+ release and CICR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ca2+ release induced in mouse oocytes by photorelease of Ins(1,4,5)P3 is a complex process involving a small initial release of Ca2+ from the Ins(1,3,4,5)-P4 sensitive pool, followed by a more substantial CICR.
the InsP3-induced release from the stores is a necessary but not sufficient event for a Ca2+ signal in mouse ovarian oocyte.
in mouse oocyte the InsP3-induced transient is not sufficient for the activation of the egg.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the InsP3-induced release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores in mouse oocytes is followed by a Ca2+-dependent Ca2+ release, which is responsible for the sustained elevation of the cytosolic Ca(2+) level.
the Ca(2+) release from intracellular stores is a very dynamic process, and it is not a simple, all or nothing, phenomenon.
the mouse oocyte is a good system to study CICR.
